evidence.note: Runs the ccc binary on individual wacc and gcc-torture test files to isolate specific failures rather than relying on the full suite — a fine-grained check.
Reads the specific failing test's C source and inspects the associated expected assembly (.s) files (data_on_page_boundary.s), i.e. inspecting emitted/expected assembly to diagnose.

After isolating and inspecting assembly again (step 56), applies a fix, rebuilds, and re-runs the single test (step 59) before returning to the full suite (step 61) — a tight per-failure verification loop.
Full 780-test suite is run only intermittently as the coarse gate, with targeted single-test checks in between.

reasoning: The agent goes beyond only running the full suite (0) and beyond guess-and-recompile (3): it isolates individual failing tests, reads their sources, and inspects expected/generated assembly, then re-verifies the single test after a fix before scaling to the full run — matching level-5 subset checking plus level-8 elements (assembly inspection, per-failure isolation, verifying before scaling). However it relies on existing test files rather than crafting deliberate minimal C reproductions and builds no reusable bisection/categorization infrastructure, so it falls short of 8/10, landing at 6.
